sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Okay, just gonna record.
sentences.zh: 好的，准备录音了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And that is producer Mark Bramhill recording himself.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人马克·布兰希尔在录他自己。

sentences.en: It is Monday, November 7th, 2016.
sentences.zh: 今天是2016年11月7日，星期一。

sentences.en: So what's happening here?
sentences.zh: 所以这里在发生什么？

sentences.en: Where are you?
sentences.zh: 你在哪儿？

sentences.en: What is going on in this tape?
sentences.zh: 这个录音里到底怎么回事？

sentences.en: So I was getting ready to go to IBM's headquarters in San Jose, California.
sentences.zh: 当时我正准备去加州圣何塞的IBM总部。

sentences.en: I was going to give this presentation to about 20 people.
sentences.zh: 我要向大约20人做这个演示。

sentences.en: I'm way more nervous than I thought I would be, but it's happening.
sentences.zh: 我比想象中紧张得多，但还是要上了。

sentences.en: So I'm just gonna practice running through the little planned script I have.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算练习过一遍我准备好的计划脚本。

sentences.en: So tell us what this presentation is about.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲这个演示是关于什么的吧。

sentences.en: So I was getting ready to make a presentation for something that, if it was approved,
sentences.zh: 当时我正准备为一个提案做演示，如果这个提案获批的话，

sentences.en: would be used by millions of people all around the world.
sentences.zh: 它将被全世界数以百万计的人使用。

sentences.en: It would change every last cell phone, tablet, and laptop all around the world.
sentences.zh: 它将改变全世界的每一部手机、平板电脑和笔记本电脑。

sentences.en: All right, I'm sold.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我被说服了。

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so it was a proposal for a brand new emoji.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一个全新表情符号的提案。

sentences.en: You know, those little pictograms we use to text each other, the thumbs up, the woman dancing,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是我们在发短信时用的那些小象形图，比如点赞、跳舞的女人，

sentences.en: or the little yellow faces that smile or wink or they wear sunglasses.
sentences.zh: 或者微笑、眨眼、戴墨镜的黄色小圆脸。

sentences.en: Okay, I know what an emoji is, Mark.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我知道什么是表情符号，马克。

sentences.en: Jeez, I'm not that old.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我没那么老。

sentences.en: You sound so nervous.
sentences.zh: 你听起来太紧张了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: It's really, really embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 这真的很尴尬、非常尴尬。

sentences.en: I'll let you know how it goes.
sentences.zh: 我之后会告诉你进展如何。

sentences.en: Okay, so before you tell us what your emoji was and whether it got approved,
sentences.zh: 好啦，在你告诉我们你的表情符号是什么以及它是否获批之前，

sentences.en: I feel like we should start with something like...
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们应该从类似这样的问题开始……

sentences.en: Why am I doing this whole thing?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要搞这一出？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Why are you doing this whole thing?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要搞这一出？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, creating an emoji, it was not something that I actually planned on doing.
sentences.zh: 所以，制作一个表情符号其实并不是我原本计划要做的事。

sentences.en: But you do cover this stuff.
sentences.zh: 但你确实在报道这些内容。

sentences.en: You have a podcast called Welcome to Macintosh.
sentences.zh: 你有一个播客叫《欢迎来到麦金塔》。

sentences.en: You cover things like the intersection of tech and culture, and so this seems to be part of your beat.
sentences.zh: 你报道科技与文化的交融之类的主题，所以这似乎在你的报道范围内。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think emoji, they're kind of right at that intersection.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我觉得表情符号正好处于那个交汇点上。

sentences.en: They've become this really interesting part of the way that we communicate.
sentences.zh: 它们已经成为我们交流方式中非常有趣的一部分。

sentences.en: They're this kind of universally spoken language of pictures.
sentences.zh: 它们是一种普遍使用的图片语言。

sentences.en: But going into all this, I didn't really know that much about emoji.
sentences.zh: 但在深入了解这一切之前，我对表情符号其实并不了解那么多。

sentences.en: So, I reached out to Jeremy Burge.
sentences.zh: 于是我联系了杰里米·伯奇。

sentences.en: He's the creator of Emojipedia.
sentences.zh: 他是表情符号百科的创始人。

sentences.en: My job is keeping on top of any new emojis and sort of documenting how they change over time.
sentences.zh: 我的工作是紧跟任何新表情符号，并记录它们随时间的变化。

sentences.en: So, for a real quick sort of history lesson on emoji, they started in Japan in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果来上一堂关于表情符号的极速历史课，它们是在90年代起源于日本的。

sentences.en: The first set of emojis was designed for a Japanese cell phone company by this guy named Shigetaka Kurita in 1998,
sentences.zh: 第一套表情符号是由一个叫栗田崇高的人在1998年为一家日本手机公司设计的，

sentences.en: when texting was still really new.
sentences.zh: 当时发短信还是一件很新鲜的事。

sentences.en: There was only 176 of them, and they were 12 by 12 pixels each.
sentences.zh: 当时只有176个表情符号，每个都是12乘12像素。

sentences.en: So, that's really low res for an emoji.
sentences.zh: 所以，对表情符号来说，那分辨率真的很低。

sentences.en: That's super low res.
sentences.zh: 那分辨率超级低。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But these were, like, the first images that could be sent via text message, before photos or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 但这些可以说是第一批可以通过短信发送的图像，在照片或其他类似东西出现之前。

sentences.en: If you see the Japanese ones, they've borderline no resemblance to what we see today.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看日本的那些表情符号，它们简直和我们今天看到的毫无相似之处。

sentences.en: They were sort of very basic, abstract pixel art.
sentences.zh: 它们是非常基础、抽象的像素艺术。

sentences.en: So, these super low res emojis became really popular in Japan.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些超低分辨率的表情符号在日本变得非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: And quickly, almost all Japanese text messages became dotted with these cute little pictures.
sentences.zh: 很快，几乎所有的日本短信里都点缀着这些可爱的小图片。

sentences.en: But they were still only available on Japanese cell phones.
sentences.zh: 但它们当时仍然只在日本手机上可用。

sentences.en: And depending on which carrier people in Japan were using, these emojis could be different from phone to phone.
sentences.zh: 而且根据日本人们使用的是哪家运营商，这些表情符号在不同的手机上可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: I might send you the hamburger and you might get the poo.
sentences.zh: 我可能发给你一个汉堡，而你收到的却是一团便便。

sentences.en: That's a problem.
sentences.zh: 这可就成问题了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: It seems like in our modern world of computers, this should not be happening.
sentences.zh: 在我们的现代计算机世界里，这似乎不应该发生。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the reason that this was happening was that when different cell carriers in Japan added these images for their customers,
sentences.zh: 但之所以会发生这种情况，是因为日本不同的手机运营商在为客户添加这些图像时，

sentences.en: they encoded them differently.
sentences.zh: 对它们的编码方式不同。

sentences.en: So, let me take just a minute to explain what character encoding is.
sentences.zh: 所以，请允许我花一分钟时间解释一下什么是字符编码。

sentences.en: This is Mark Davis.
sentences.zh: 这位是马克·戴维斯。

sentences.en: Every time you see a character on the screen, on your mobile or laptop, it's always represented internally by a number.
sentences.zh: 每次你在屏幕上看到一个字符，无论是在手机还是笔记本电脑上，它在内部总是用一个数字来表示。

sentences.en: So, there's some number associated with the letter A.
sentences.zh: 所以，字母A会对应着某个数字。

sentences.en: So, the problem in Japan was that the companies weren't coordinating about what emojis were assigned to what number.
sentences.zh: 所以在日本出现的问题是，各家公司没有就哪个表情符号分配给哪个数字进行协调。

sentences.en: So, one company might have the hamburger encoded as 46,790, while another carrier would have the poo encoded as 46,790.
sentences.zh: 因此，一家公司可能把汉堡编码为46,790，而另一家运营商可能把便便编码为46,790。

sentences.en: So, when American cell phone companies decided that they wanted to enter the Japanese market,
sentences.zh: 所以，当美国手机公司决定进军日本市场时，

sentences.en: they knew that they needed the coding for these emojis to become standardized.
sentences.zh: 他们知道自己需要让这些表情符号的编码实现标准化。

sentences.en: And they turned to Mark and his organization, a group called the Unicode Consortium.
sentences.zh: 于是他们找到了马克和他的组织，一个名为统一码联盟的团体。

sentences.en: I'm the president of the Unicode Consortium.
sentences.zh: 我是统一码联盟的主席。

sentences.en: We're people behind the curtains, making sure that everything works.
sentences.zh: 我们是幕后工作者，确保一切正常运转。

sentences.en: It's kind of like plumbers, you know.
sentences.zh: 这有点像水管工，你知道的。

sentences.en: You don't notice them as long as the water keeps flowing.
sentences.zh: 只要水一直在流，你就不会注意到他们。

sentences.en: They're doing the 99% invisible work of the internet, if you will.
sentences.zh: 可以说，他们做的是互联网上那99%不为人知的隐形工作。

sentences.en: I guess I'll allow it.
sentences.zh: 我想我姑且批准这种说法吧。

sentences.en: So, the Unicode Consortium had already been working on standardization for a while.
sentences.zh: 所以，统一码联盟其实已经致力于标准化工作一段时间了。

sentences.en: Not with emoji, but with text.
sentences.zh: 不是针对表情符号，而是针对文本。

sentences.en: The consortium was founded back in the early days of the internet,
sentences.zh: 该联盟早在互联网早期就成立了，

sentences.en: when there was no universal standard for encoding text or anything else you saw online.
sentences.zh: 当时对于文本或你在网上看到的任何其他内容，还没有通用的编码标准。

sentences.en: People at the time were really used to getting emails or looking at websites,
sentences.zh: 当时的人们非常习惯于收电子邮件或浏览网站，

sentences.en: and they would see just jumbled up garbage on the screen because it was the wrong encoding.
sentences.zh: 结果在屏幕上只看到一堆乱码，因为编码错误。

sentences.en: The internet used to be so ugly.
sentences.zh: 以前的互联网太丑了。

sentences.en: Like, when you were a baby, you don't even know.
sentences.zh: 就像你还是个婴儿的时候，你甚至都不知道。

sentences.en: The internet was terrible then.
sentences.zh: 那时的互联网太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I have heard stories.
sentences.zh: 对，我听说过一些故事。

sentences.en: But, you know, Unicode, they were founded to help with that.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道的，统一码联盟成立就是为了帮助解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Most of their work has to do with language.
sentences.zh: 他们的大部分工作都与语言有关。

sentences.en: You know, making sure that even little-known languages are legible across different websites and platforMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，要确保即使是鲜为人知的语言也能在不同的网站和平台上清晰显示。

sentences.en: That seems totally fair.
sentences.zh: 这听起来完全合情合理。

sentences.en: Make the World Wide Web worldwide.
sentences.zh: 让万维网真正走向世界。

sentences.en: Make sure everyone can be represented.
sentences.zh: 确保每个人都能被代表。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And ultimately, Unicode became the be-all, end-all text encoding standard.
sentences.zh: 最终，统一码成为了终极的文本编码标准。

sentences.en: So, since people were already relying on Unicode standardized text encoding,
sentences.zh: 所以，既然人们已经依赖统一码的标准化文本编码，

sentences.en: they thought, why don't we get these guys to do emojis for us, too?
sentences.zh: 他们就在想，为什么不让这群人也帮我们搞定表情符号呢？

sentences.en: Yes, yes, precisely.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，确切地说。

sentences.en: Though, when Unicode was first approached about emojis in the early 2000s, they weren't interested.
sentences.zh: 不过，在2000年代初首次有人就表情符号接触统一码时，他们并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: They thought that these cute little pictures, they're probably a passing fad.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这些可爱的小图片可能只是一时的潮流。

sentences.en: I think we were all kind of hoping and praying for that, too.
sentences.zh: 我想我们当时也都在某种程度上这样期盼和祈祷着。

sentences.en: No, Robin, no.
sentences.zh: 不，罗宾，不。

sentences.en: Emojis are here to stay.
sentences.zh: 表情符号会一直存在下去。

sentences.en: And five years later, around 2006, Unicode realized emojis were not going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 五年后，大约在2006年，统一码意识到表情符号不会消失。

sentences.en: So, they decided to take on the project of standardizing them.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定承担起将其实施标准化的项目。

sentences.en: So, they looked at all the different emoji that had been created by the Japanese carriers
sentences.zh: 因此，他们查看了日本运营商创建的所有不同表情符号，

sentences.en: and sorted through them to establish an initial core library.
sentences.zh: 并对其进行分类筛选，以建立一个最初的核心库。

sentences.en: So, what was in that original set of emojis?
sentences.zh: 那么，最初那一套表情符号里都有什么？

sentences.en: It was kind of a hodgepodge.
sentences.zh: 那算是一个大杂烩。

sentences.en: You know, two camels, four mailboxes, five trains.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，两头骆驼、四个邮箱、五列火车。

sentences.en: Well, you need two camels because you've got the one hump and the two hump.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你需要两头骆驼，因为单峰驼和双峰驼你都得有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's important.
sentences.zh: 这很重要。

sentences.en: It's really important.
sentences.zh: 这真的很重要。

sentences.en: And so, once they had that core library, Unicode decided that all additional emojis should be
sentences.zh: 所以，一旦有了这个核心库，统一码决定，所有新增的表情符号都应该

sentences.en: considered very carefully and voted on and approved by Davis and the rest of the consortium.
sentences.zh: 经过非常仔细的考虑，并由戴维斯和联盟的其他成员投票表决通过。

sentences.en: No more two camels slipping through the cracks.
sentences.zh: 再也没有那种漏网的两头骆驼了。

sentences.en: Each emoji that we encode, we really have to think, does this sort of break new ground?
sentences.zh: 我们编码的每一个表情符号，我们真的都必须思考：这算开辟新天地吗？

sentences.en: Does it go in a new direction?
sentences.zh: 它朝着新的方向发展了吗？

sentences.en: Is it going to be extremely popular?
sentences.zh: 它会极其受欢迎吗？

sentences.en: Because we know that faces, for example, are very popular.
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道，比如说，脸部表情非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: You know, the hearts are very popular and so on.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，爱心非常受欢迎，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, we try to weigh all these factors when we pick a set.
sentences.zh: 所以在挑选一套表情时，我们会努力权衡所有这些因素。

sentences.en: So, these guys really do pick all the emojis that are on my phone, that they are the ones who decide.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人真的是在挑选我手机上的所有表情符号，他们才是做决定的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: So, four times a year, Unicode meets to consider all the proposals they have for new emojis.
sentences.zh: 因此，统一码联盟每年开会四次，审议他们收到的所有新表情符号提案。

sentences.en: And they are the final say in which ones are approved.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有哪些表情符号获批的最终决定权。

sentences.en: And once an emoji is approved, it never goes away.
sentences.zh: 而且一旦一个表情符号获批，它就永远不会消失。

sentences.en: Emoji can only be added.
sentences.zh: 表情符号只能增加。

sentences.en: Once an emoji, always an emoji, you know?
sentences.zh: 一旦成为表情符号，就永远是表情符号，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And so, who comes up with these new ideas for emojis?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些关于表情符号的新点子都是谁想出来的？

sentences.en: Like, who gets to submit proposals?
sentences.zh: 比如说，谁有资格提交提案？

sentences.en: So, I had this question, too.
sentences.zh: 所以，我也有这个疑问。

sentences.en: And I asked Jeremy, the guy from Emojipedia.
sentences.zh: 我问了杰里米，也就是来自表情符号百科的那个人。

sentences.en: And this is what turned this story from idle curiosity into a year-long journey.
sentences.zh: 而正是这一点，让这个故事从闲极无聊的好奇心变成了一场长达一年的旅程。

sentences.en: For the proposals, like, who is actually responsible for bringing these emoji into the world?
sentences.zh: 关于提案，具体来说，到底是谁负责将这些表情符号带到这个世界上？

sentences.en: Literally anybody, anyone on the planet.
sentences.zh: 字面意义上的任何人，地球上的任何人。

sentences.en: You could send a proposal in right now, and Unicode would look at it, and there's a chance that it could become an actual emoji.
sentences.zh: 你现在就可以发一份提案过来，统一码会审阅它，它就有机会成为一个真正的表情符号。

sentences.en: So, like, I could do this.
sentences.zh: 所以，也就是说我可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Like, I could send a proposal in.
sentences.zh: 比如，我可以提交一份提案。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, of course, when Jeremy told me that, I knew that I had to submit a proposal for an emoji.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然啦，当杰里米告诉我这一点时，我知道我必须提交一份表情符号提案。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然咯。

sentences.en: Yeah, clearly.
sentences.zh: 对，显然如此。

sentences.en: What better way to understand the process than to go through it myself?
sentences.zh: 还有什么比亲自走一遍流程更好的方式来理解它呢？

sentences.en: But I didn't really have an idea for what I wanted to propose.
sentences.zh: 但我其实并不知道自己想提议什么。

sentences.en: So Jeremy gave me a few basic guidelines to think about.
sentences.zh: 所以杰里米给了我一些需要思考的基本准则。

sentences.en: You should be trying to prove there's already demand before you got involved.
sentences.zh: 你应该努力证明在你参与之前就已经有需求了。

sentences.en: Don't start a petition and generate demand.
sentences.zh: 不要去发起请愿来凭空制造需求。

sentences.en: He said that Unicode wants people writing proposals to cite evidence of demand, like hashtag usage on Twitter or Instagram or Google search trends.
sentences.zh: 他说，统一码联盟希望提交提案的人能够引用需求证据，比如推特、Instagram 或谷歌搜索趋势上的标签使用情况。

sentences.en: He also said that my proposed emoji should be visually distinctive.
sentences.zh: 他还说，我提议的表情符号在视觉上必须具有辨识度。

sentences.en: If it looks the same as something else, it doesn't matter if it means something different emojis about what they look like.
sentences.zh: 如果它看起来和别的差不多，那即使含义不同也没什么意义，关于表情符号，大家首先看的是外表。

sentences.en: But it can't be too specific.
sentences.zh: 但它又不能太具体。

sentences.en: Like, it can't be for this one really specific kind of dinosaur or whatever.
sentences.zh: 比如，它不能是针对某种非常具体的恐龙之类的东西。

sentences.en: And at the opposite end of the spectrum, it can't be too vague.
sentences.zh: 而在相反的极端，它又不能太含糊。

sentences.en: You know, if your emoji was just dinosaur, you might need more specificity, like T-Rex.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你的表情符号仅仅是恐龙，你可能就需要更具体一点，比如霸王龙。

sentences.en: Well, it's a pretty fine line, but I think I get it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一个相当微妙的界限，但我想我明白了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Another thing, they don't want to add an emoji that's potentially just a fad.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事，他们不想添加一个可能只是一时流行的表情符号。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I get that.
sentences.zh: 我懂这个。

sentences.en: So you don't want an emoji of like a, I don't know, like a fidget spinner or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以你不会想要一个像，我不知道，比如指尖陀螺或类似东西的表情符号。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，对，没错。

sentences.en: Fidget spinners, who knows how long those will be around.
sentences.zh: 指尖陀螺，谁知道这东西能火多久。

sentences.en: You also can't submit logos or brands, specific people, deities, etc.
sentences.zh: 你也不能提交徽标或品牌、特定人物、神灵等。

sentences.en: Superman and Batman, Starbucks, and those are just not going to be included.
sentences.zh: 超人和蝙蝠侠、星巴克，这些都是不会被收录的。

sentences.en: They have to be generic.
sentences.zh: 它们必须是通用的。

sentences.en: So there are already like a few thousand emojis, right?
sentences.zh: 所以现在已经有好几千个表情符号了，对吧？

sentences.en: There's 2,666 as of recording, but.
sentences.zh: 截至录制时有2,666个，不过。

sentences.en: Well, there you go.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那就对了。

sentences.en: So if you're not going to do Batman and Superman, what doesn't exist yet that you could actually propose?
sentences.zh: 既然你不打算做蝙蝠侠和超人，那还有什么目前不存在、而你实际上可以提议的呢？

sentences.en: So I actually asked Jeremy this.
sentences.zh: 所以我其实问过杰里米这个问题。

sentences.en: What do people really, really want?
sentences.zh: 人们真正、真正想要的是什么？

sentences.en: And this is what he told me.
sentences.zh: 这就是他告诉我的。

sentences.en: So there is yoga because it's a popular activity that a lot of people around the world do.
sentences.zh: 这里有瑜伽，因为这是一项全球许多人都在做的热门活动。

sentences.en: If somebody decided to submit yoga and or meditating, I think that would be quite the winner.
sentences.zh: 如果有人决定提交瑜伽和/或冥想，我认为那绝对会是个大赢家。

sentences.en: So, I'll be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，老实说。

sentences.en: I had never done yoga.
sentences.zh: 我从未练过瑜伽。

sentences.en: I had never meditated.
sentences.zh: 我从未进行过冥想。

sentences.en: I didn't have particularly strong feelings about either one.
sentences.zh: 我对这两者都没有特别强烈的感觉。

sentences.en: But I wanted to pitch an emoji.
sentences.zh: 但我想推出一个表情符号。

sentences.en: And this had good odds of being approved, so.
sentences.zh: 而且这个被批准的几率很大，所以。

sentences.en: Namaste, motherf***ers.
sentences.zh: 合十礼，你们这些混蛋。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, I went full namaste on this.
sentences.zh: 对，对，我在这个上面彻底开启了合十礼模式。

sentences.en: Started doing all kinds of research about yoga and meditation.
sentences.zh: 开始对瑜伽和冥想进行各种研究。

sentences.en: Did you know, for example, Roman, that there are 35 million Instagram posts with hashtag yoga compared to hashtag running's paltry 31 million?
sentences.zh: 罗曼，举个例子，你知道带有“瑜伽”标签的 Instagram 帖子有 3500 万条，而“跑步”标签只有区区 3100 万条吗？

sentences.en: Well, clearly that means there has to be an emoji for yoga.
sentences.zh: 好吧，很显然这意味着必须有一个瑜伽的表情符号。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What would you use to represent that?
sentences.zh: 你会用什么来代表它？

sentences.en: So, I actually decided to go with an image that I felt represented both meditation and yoga.
sentences.zh: 所以，我其实决定采用一个我认为既能代表冥想又能代表瑜伽的形象。

sentences.en: A person in lotus pose.
sentences.zh: 一个盘腿打坐的人。

sentences.en: And that's the one where you said cross-legged and you have your hands, like, face up on each knee, right?
sentences.zh: 就是那种你说盘腿坐着，然后双手掌心朝上放在各自身上，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，对，没错。

sentences.en: The sort of famous cross-legged sitting pose, yeah.
sentences.zh: 那种著名的盘腿坐姿，对。

sentences.en: And so, I found some clip art on the internet to illustrate what the emoji might look like.
sentences.zh: 于是，我在互联网上找到了一些剪贴画来演示这个表情符号可能会是什么样子。

sentences.en: And in the end, I put together this eight-page proposal to submit to Unicode.
sentences.zh: 最后，我整理了这份八页的提案提交给统一码联盟。

sentences.en: I felt pretty good about it, but I wanted to run it by someone who had actually gone through the process.
sentences.zh: 我对它感觉挺满意，但我想把它拿给一个真正经历过这个流程的人过目一下。

sentences.en: My name is Jennifer Eight Lee, and I successfully proposed a dumpling emoji.
sentences.zh: 我叫黄仁娥，我成功提议了一个饺子表情符号。

sentences.en: Her middle name is actually the number eight, which is so cool.
sentences.zh: 她的中间名其实就是数字八，太酷了。

sentences.en: And she was actually in an episode that we did about fortune cookies a while back.
sentences.zh: 她之前还上过我们不久前做的一期关于幸运饼干的节目。

sentences.en: Yeah, and she actually successfully made a fortune cookie emoji as well.
sentences.zh: 对，而且她其实也成功制作了一个幸运饼干表情符号。

sentences.en: Anyway, back in 2015, when Lee was working on getting the dumpling emoji added into Unicode,
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，早在2015年，当黄仁娥致力于将饺子表情符号加入统一码时，

sentences.en: she learned that Unicode is this non-profit, but it is controlled by a small handful of tech companies.
sentences.zh: 她了解到统一码是一个非营利组织，但它是由一小撮科技公司控制的。

sentences.en: You know, at that point, it had 11 full voting members that paid $18,000 a year to vote.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时它有11个拥有完全投票权的成员，他们每年支付18,000美元来获得投票权。

sentences.en: So, of those 11, eight of them were U.S.
sentences.zh: 在这11个成员中，有8个是美国

sentences.en: multinational tech companies.
sentences.zh: 跨国科技公司。

sentences.en: So, it's Oracle, IBM, Google, Apple, Facebook, Yahoo, Microsoft, and Adobe.
sentences.zh: 它们是甲骨文、IBM、谷歌、苹果、脸书、雅虎、微软和Adobe。

sentences.en: So, those were the eight.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是那八个。

sentences.en: Of the other three, they were the German software company, SAP,
sentences.zh: 至于其他三个，它们分别是德国软件公司思爱普，

sentences.en: the Chinese telecom company, Huawei, and the government of Oman.
sentences.zh: 中国电信公司华为，以及阿曼政府。

sentences.en: Did she say the government of Oman?
sentences.zh: 她刚刚说阿曼政府？

sentences.en: Yeah, because remember, most of what Unicode does has nothing to do with emoji,
sentences.zh: 对，因为记住，统一码所做的大部分工作与表情符号毫无关系，

sentences.en: and mostly to do with encoding language on the internet.
sentences.zh: 主要与互联网上的语言编码有关。

sentences.en: So, the government of Oman is there to advocate for greater Arabic language support on computers.
sentences.zh: 所以，阿曼政府在那里是为了倡导在计算机上获得更好的阿拉伯语支持。

sentences.en: Oh, that makes total sense.
sentences.zh: 哦，那完全说得通。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And now, Lee is a part of the emoji subcommittee with Unicode.
sentences.zh: 现在，黄仁娥是统一码表情符号小组委员会的成员。

sentences.en: She can't vote on which emoji get approved, but she is able to help novices like myself
sentences.zh: 她不能对哪些表情符号获得批准进行投票，但她能够帮助像我这样的新手

sentences.en: navigate the difficult path to emoji land.
sentences.zh: 在通往表情符号大陆的艰难道路上导航。

sentences.en: So, I showed her my proposal.
sentences.zh: 所以，我把我的提案给她看了。

sentences.en: It looks pretty solid.
sentences.zh: 看起来相当扎实。

sentences.en: Yes!
sentences.zh: 太棒了！

sentences.en: But I think your emoji characters are a little bit ugly.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你的表情符号有点丑。

sentences.en: No!
sentences.zh: 不会吧！

sentences.en: Well, you did use clip art, man.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你确实用了剪贴画，老兄。

sentences.en: That's fair, fair.
sentences.zh: 这倒也是，这倒也是。

sentences.en: Probably not the standard of emoji characters, so I don't know where you got them,
sentences.zh: 这可能达不到表情符号的标准，我不知道你是从哪弄来的，

sentences.en: but you might do them in more of, like, either the Apple style or more of the Google style.
sentences.zh: 但你或许应该把它做得更偏向苹果风格，或者更偏向谷歌风格一些。

sentences.en: She was right.
sentences.zh: 她说得对。

sentences.en: I mean, my design was not great.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我的设计确实不咋地。

sentences.en: So, I ditched these clip art images and hired a professional, a woman named Afi Messer,
sentences.zh: 所以，我抛弃了这些剪贴画，雇佣了一位专业人士，一个名叫阿菲·梅瑟的女人，

sentences.en: just so that my case would be stronger and Unicode would have a better idea of what this emoji could look like.
sentences.zh: 只是为了让我的案例更有说服力，也让统一码能更好地了解这个表情符号会长什么样。

sentences.en: I polished up my proposal, named it Person Meditating, and submitted it.
sentences.zh: 我润色了我的提案，将其命名为“打坐的人”，然后提交了上去。

sentences.en: Right at the deadline.
sentences.zh: 就在截止日期前。

sentences.en: And then, a few weeks later.
sentences.zh: 然后，几个星期后。

sentences.en: So, I'm just coming into the studio now.
sentences.zh: 所以，我现在正走进录音室。

sentences.en: I just got an email from Unicode.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚收到一封来自统一码的电子邮件。

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 我来看看。

sentences.en: Let me load it up.
sentences.zh: 让我把它打开。

sentences.en: It says,
sentences.zh: 上面写着：

sentences.en: The Emoji Subcommittee has decided to forward your proposal to the UTC.
sentences.zh: 表情符号小组委员会已决定将您的提案转交给UTC（统一码技术委员会）。

sentences.en: The document number will be L2 slash 16 dash 279.
sentences.zh: 文件编号将是 L2 斜杠 16 斜杠 279。

sentences.en: Regards, UTC.
sentences.zh: 致礼，UTC。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Woo!
sentences.zh: 哇哦！

sentences.en: So, that sounds like good news, but what does that actually mean?
sentences.zh: 听起来是个好消息，但这到底意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: It basically means that I got through the first round, that Unicode was going to hold an official vote on my emoji.
sentences.zh: 这基本上意味着我通过了第一轮，统一码将对我的表情符号进行正式投票。

sentences.en: And at this point, you know, you can sit back and see what happens.
sentences.zh: 而在此时，你知道，你可以高高挂起，静观其变。

sentences.en: Or, if you are extra excited, like I was, you can actually show up to a quarterly meeting of the Unicode Technical Committee and present your proposal in real life.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果你格外激动，就像我一样，你实际上可以亲自出席统一码技术委员会的季度会议，在现实生活中展示你的提案。

sentences.en: And so, that brings us back to you being super nervous before your presentation back in November.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带回了你在11月演讲前超级紧张的状态。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: It is Monday, November 7th, 2016.
sentences.zh: 今天是2016年11月7日，星期一。

sentences.en: And today is the day that I'm presenting to the Unicode Technical Committee.
sentences.zh: 今天是我向统一码技术委员会做演示的日子。

sentences.en: But, before we get to that, I want to talk about someone I met while I was there in the Bay Area.
sentences.zh: 但是，在我们谈到这个之前，我想聊聊我在湾区时遇到的一个人。

sentences.en: She was also there to make a presentation to Unicode.
sentences.zh: 她也是去向统一码做演示的。

sentences.en: Her name is Rayouf Alhumadi.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫雷乌夫·阿尔胡马迪。

sentences.en: My name is Rayouf Alhumadi.
sentences.zh: 我叫雷乌夫·阿尔胡马迪。

sentences.en: I'm 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 我15岁。

sentences.en: She's 15 years old, like in high school, and she wrote up one of these proposals like you did?
sentences.zh: 她15岁，就像在读高中一样，她也像你一样写了其中一份提案？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Believe me, this is no small task.
sentences.zh: 相信我，这绝非易事。

sentences.en: I have never written any proposals whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有写过任何提案。

sentences.en: The closest thing I've done were lab reports and science class.
sentences.zh: 我做过最接近的事就是在科学课上写实验报告。

sentences.en: But for Rayouf, this whole thing just had a totally different level of importance.
sentences.zh: 但对雷乌夫来说，整件事有着完全不同层面的重要性。

sentences.en: You mean that some people do this not just to make a cool radio story out of it?
sentences.zh: 你的意思是有些人做这件事不只是为了把它做成一个很酷的广播故事？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, you know, because emojis represent culture.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对，你知道的，因为表情符号代表了文化。

sentences.en: And just like it matters to see a representation of your culture in television or movies,
sentences.zh: 正如在电视或电影中看到对你文化的代表很重要一样，

sentences.en: seeing yourself in an emoji can feel important in the same way.
sentences.zh: 在表情符号中看到自己也会以同样的方式让人觉得很重要。

sentences.en: I mean, humans all over the world send something like six billion of these little things to each other every day.
sentences.zh: 我是说，全世界的人类每天都在互相发送大约六十亿个这样的小东西。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: They're everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它们无处不在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so, in the last five years, Unicode has tried to represent more people by adding characters with a range of different skin tones.
sentences.zh: 所以在过去五年里，统一码试图通过添加具有各种不同肤色的字符来代表更多的人。

sentences.en: They've added some gay characters and a few gender-neutral, androgynous ones as well.
sentences.zh: 他们还添加了一些同性恋字符以及一些中性、雌雄同体的字符。

sentences.en: But there was still no one that looked like Rayouf, because she wears a hijab.
sentences.zh: 但仍然没有人长得像雷乌夫，因为她戴着头巾。

sentences.en: I felt like, you know, it would be nice for me to see, have an emoji of myself on the keyboards that I could use.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，你知道，如果我能看到，能在键盘上有一个我自己的表情符号并且可以使用，那会很棒。

sentences.en: Rayouf felt like her emoji would help other women who wear hijabs feel more represented in mainstream culture.
sentences.zh: 雷乌夫觉得她的表情符号将有助于让其他戴头巾的女性在主流文化中感受到更多的代表性。

sentences.en: Even though it is something small, I think it will, you know, just normalize the hijab.
sentences.zh: 即使这是一件小事，我认为它也会，你知道的，让头巾变得正常化。

sentences.en: You'll definitely be, definitely be the coolest, like, coolest kid.
sentences.zh: 你绝对会成为，绝对会成为最酷的，最酷的孩子。

sentences.en: Like, if it does pass, I just told my friends, we're going to have to celebrate.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果它真的通过了，我刚告诉我的朋友们，我们必须庆祝一下。

sentences.en: Like, I'm going to bring cupcakes of the emoji to school for everybody, even for the teachers, because it would be something so amazing if hopefully it does pass.
sentences.zh: 比如，我要带印有这个表情符号的纸杯蛋糕到学校分给大家，甚至分给老师，因为如果它真的能通过，那将是一件非常了不起的事情。

sentences.en: Well, now I'm totally rooting for Rayouf.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在我完全在支持雷乌夫了。

sentences.en: They can choose more than one, Robin.
sentences.zh: 他们可以选不止一个，罗宾。

sentences.en: You can root for us both.
sentences.zh: 你可以同时支持我们俩。

sentences.en: Yeah, but if it's between you and her, it's definitely her.
sentences.zh: 对，但如果非要在你和她之间选一个，那绝对是她。

sentences.en: Okay, that's fair.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这很公平。

sentences.en: That's fair.
sentences.zh: 这很公平。

sentences.en: So, Rayouf and I were both presenting to Unicode on the same day.
sentences.zh: 所以，雷乌夫和我是在同一天向统一码做演示的。

sentences.en: I'll be presenting at 2.
sentences.zh: 我将在2点做演示。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm presenting at 11.30.
sentences.zh: 哦，我是在11点30分做演示。

sentences.en: Okay, so I'll miss you then.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那到时候我就错过你的了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: When it was my turn, they made me turn off my microphone.
sentences.zh: 轮到我的时候，他们让我关掉了麦克风。

sentences.en: So, I don't have tape of what I said, but basically I gave a little spiel about why the world was in dire need of a yoga emoji.
sentences.zh: 所以，我没有我发言的录音，但基本上我发表了一番简短的演讲，讲的是为什么世界迫切需要一个瑜伽表情符号。

sentences.en: I got a few laughs, some nodding heads.
sentences.zh: 我引起了一些笑声，还有人点头。

sentences.en: It lasted about five minutes, and then I took a few questions.
sentences.zh: 大约持续了五分钟，然后我回答了几个问题。

sentences.en: After it was over, I stood there kind of waiting for some indication of whether, you know, the committee liked it.
sentences.zh: 结束后，我站在那儿等着，想看看委员会是否，你知道的，喜欢它。

sentences.en: And did they like it?
sentences.zh: 那他们喜欢吗？

sentences.en: They wouldn't say.
sentences.zh: 他们不说。

sentences.en: Finally, someone told me, basically, you need to leave so we can vote.
sentences.zh: 最后，有人基本上告诉我，你得离开，这样我们才能投票。

sentences.en: And so, I left, and I just figured that they'd be in touch soon.
sentences.zh: 所以，我离开了，我当时想他们很快就会联系我。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, if your emoji is approved, then what happens next?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你的表情符号被批准了，接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: So, even though I submitted this really beautiful visual for my person meditating emoji, it's really more just to demonstrate what it could look like.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管我为打坐的人这个表情符号提交了一张非常漂亮的视觉图，但这其实更多只是为了展示它可能长什么样。

sentences.en: And ultimately, if the emoji is approved,
sentences.zh: 归根结底，如果这个表情符号获批，

sentences.en: Google and Facebook and Apple and all the other platforms will get to decide what exactly person meditating looks like in their own platform style.
sentences.zh: 谷歌、Facebook、苹果和所有其他平台都将自行决定打坐的人在各自的平台风格中到底长什么样。

sentences.en: So, I talked to someone from Google about this.
sentences.zh: 为此，我跟谷歌的一位员工聊了聊。

sentences.en: My name's Rachel Bean.
sentences.zh: 我叫雷切尔·宾。

sentences.en: I'm a creative director at Google on the material design team.
sentences.zh: 我是谷歌材料设计团队的创意总监。

sentences.en: But she has another title, too.
sentences.zh: 但她还有另一个头衔。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: I am also, funnily enough, the creative director of emoji at Google.
sentences.zh: 说来有趣，我同时也是谷歌表情符号的创意总监。

sentences.en: Once Rachel Bean and her team get the list of new emojis and their codes from Unicode, they'll design the images to be used on all of Google's Android phones.
sentences.zh: 一旦雷切尔·宾和她的团队从统一码联盟拿到新表情符号及其代码的列表，他们就会设计出用于谷歌所有安卓手机的图像。

sentences.en: And what kind of guidance do they get from Unicode about how to draw them, how to make them look?
sentences.zh: 那他们从统一码联盟那里得到了什么样的指导，比如怎么画，怎么让它们看起来像？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, they don't actually give them all that much.
sentences.zh: 所以，其实他们并没有给太多指导。

sentences.en: They give them the name of the emoji and a few keywords of things it might represent.
sentences.zh: 他们只给出了表情符号的名字和几个可能代表它的关键词。

sentences.en: You know, occasionally, they might give a little bit of guidance of, you know, the bagel emoji, it should be drawn sliced so that people won't confuse it with the donut.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，偶尔他们可能会给一点点指导，比如说，百吉饼表情符号应该画成切开的，这样人们就不会把它和甜甜圈搞混了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, that makes it so that Google emojis look different from Apple emojis and they look different from Twitter emojis.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就使得谷歌的表情符号看起来和苹果的表情符号不同，也和推特的表情符号不同。

sentences.en: They're all really different.
sentences.zh: 它们真的各不相同。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: Obviously, characters might be facing in a different direction or have different outfits on or maybe dance in another style.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，角色的朝向可能会不同，穿的衣服也可能不同，或者跳舞的风格也不一样。

sentences.en: But they should all illustrate the same basic concept.
sentences.zh: 但它们都应该阐述同一个基本概念。

sentences.en: And recently, Rachel Bean and her team at Google have redesigned the entire library of Android emojis.
sentences.zh: 最近，雷切尔·宾和她在谷歌的团队重新设计了安卓表情符号的整个库。

sentences.en: For all the emojis that weren't just disembodied faces, the team had to deeply consider all the clothing and accessories that they were wearing.
sentences.zh: 对于所有不只是独立面孔的表情符号，团队都必须深思熟虑它们所穿的服装和佩戴的配饰。

sentences.en: Because they're designing for a global audience.
sentences.zh: 因为他们是在为全球受众进行设计。

sentences.en: Take, for example, the farmer emoji.
sentences.zh: 以农夫表情符号为例。

sentences.en: Originally, we had designed the farmer emoji, very American Gothic style.
sentences.zh: 最初，我们设计的农夫表情符号是非常美式哥特风格的。

sentences.en: So, you know, a pitchfork and wearing overalls.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，拿着草叉，穿着背带裤。

sentences.en: But a lot of farmers all around the world, they don't actually use pitchforks.
sentences.zh: 但世界各地的许多农夫实际上并不使用草叉。

sentences.en: That's kind of an old and very American characterization.
sentences.zh: 那算是一种陈旧且非常美国化的角色刻画。

sentences.en: And also the overalls, to some degree, weren't necessarily the outfit that most farmers globally wear.
sentences.zh: 而且在某种程度上，背带裤也不一定全球大多数农夫都会穿。

sentences.en: So we've changed the actual prop that the farmer was holding into a grain.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把农夫手里拿的那个道具改成了谷物。

sentences.en: So to really put more emphasis on what's grown universally versus tools that may not be universally used.
sentences.zh: 这样就能真正把重点放在全球通用的东西上，而不是那些可能并非全球通用的工具上。

sentences.en: And this kind of global inclusivity is the same stuff they'll have to consider with the emoji that I proposed.
sentences.zh: 这种全球包容性，也是他们在我提议的表情符号中必须考虑的因素。

sentences.en: You know, of the person meditating.
sentences.zh: 也就是打坐的人。

sentences.en: What will it wear?
sentences.zh: 它会穿什么？

sentences.en: Like, what's the color of the clothing?
sentences.zh: 比如，衣服是什么颜色的？

sentences.en: Is he or she, are they going to be wearing leggings, a leotard, a t-shirt?
sentences.zh: 他或她，他们会穿紧身裤、连体紧身衣还是T恤？

sentences.en: You know, it's good that they're thinking about this, but the Google designers are never going to really be able to fairly represent all cultures.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们能考虑到这一点很好，但谷歌的设计师永远无法真正做到公平地代表所有文化。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Unicode is this governing body with a bunch of representatives, but they're all mostly from these big tech companies.
sentences.zh: 统一码联盟是一个由许多代表组成的管理机构，但他们大部分都来自这些大型科技公司。

sentences.en: And so this whole system, it kind of irks people.
sentences.zh: 所以整个系统，多少让人有点反感。

sentences.en: It's not a good system.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个好系统。

sentences.en: You shouldn't have to ask these people's permission.
sentences.zh: 你本不该去请求这些人的允许。

sentences.en: This is Keith Winstein.
sentences.zh: 这位是基斯·温斯坦。

sentences.en: I'm Keith Winstein.
sentences.zh: 我是基斯·温斯坦。

sentences.en: I'm an assistant professor of computer science here at Stanford.
sentences.zh: 我是斯坦福大学计算机科学系的助理教授。

sentences.en: And he says, you know, if there is not an emoji that represents you or your culture, Unicode's process for getting one is not exactly quick.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果还没有一个表情符号能代表你或你的文化，统一码联盟审批通过一个表情符号的流程可绝对算不上快。

sentences.en: So having to wait, you know, two or three years for it to end up in the standard, and that's a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以你得等上两三年才能最终纳入标准，这可是一段很长的时间。

sentences.en: It doesn't take quite that long anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在其实不需要等那么久了。

sentences.en: It's closer to one or two years.
sentences.zh: 接近一两年吧。

sentences.en: But still, Winstein points out that there are already platforms like Slack that let you take an image and make it emoji-sized, where you don't need to go through Unicode.
sentences.zh: 不过，温斯坦指出，现在已经有了像Slack这样的平台，允许你拿一张图片并把它做成表情符号的大小，这样你就不需要通过统一码联盟了。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally, because Kurt Kolstad on our staff, he does this, and he makes a little emoji for every episode, and we share it when the episode comes out.
sentences.zh: 对，完全是这样，因为我们员工库尔特·科尔斯特ad就在这么做，他为每一集都做一个小表情符号，当单集发布时我们就分享它。

sentences.en: And it's just a little picture.
sentences.zh: 这只是一张小图片。

sentences.en: It's not really an emoji.
sentences.zh: 它其实算不上真正的表情符号。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so there is no special encoding process required to make them.
sentences.zh: 所以制作它们不需要任何特殊的编码流程。

sentences.en: This is a much simpler way of doing it, rather than trying to cram everything into Unicode.
sentences.zh: 这是一种简单得多的方法，总比非要把所有东西都塞进统一码联盟里要好。

sentences.en: And even though I think Winstein gets at some really important criticisms, if we went to a system where we really just sent tiny pictures,
sentences.zh: 尽管我认为温斯坦切中了某些非常重要的批评，但如果我们变成了一种真的只发送微小图片的系统，

sentences.en: then the thing that I really love about emojis would kind of be lost, which is that they've turned into this sort of universal, standardized language of pictures.
sentences.zh: 那么我对表情符号最热爱的那种特质就会消失了，也就是它们已经演变成了一种普遍的、标准化的图片语言。

sentences.en: Like, the idea that some stranger in Argentina and I are both sending a heart-eyes emoji to express love, I think there's something really cool about that.
sentences.zh: 比如，阿根廷的某个陌生人和我都在发送爱心眼表情符号来表达爱意，我认为这真的是一件很酷的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a nice quality to them, that they're universal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们具有普遍性，这是一个很好的特质。

sentences.en: So, um, so what happened with your meditating person?
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你的那个打坐的人后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: You must know by now.
sentences.zh: 你现在一定知道了。

sentences.en: So for a few days after my presentation, I still hadn't heard anything.
sentences.zh: 所以在我的演讲结束后的几天里，我依然没有任何消息。

sentences.en: Like, no email thanking me for my proposal, or letting me know when I'd hear back, or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 比如，没有感谢我提交提案的邮件，也没有告诉我什么时候能收到回复，或者诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: It was just total radio silence.
sentences.zh: 简直是死一般地寂静。

sentences.en: And then I was just scrolling on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 然后我就在推特上随便刷着。

sentences.en: Um, so I just saw that Emojipedia has, uh, tweeted about some of the new emoji.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我看到Emojipedia发了推文，提到了几个新的表情符号。

sentences.en: Let's see, I'm opening up the page.
sentences.zh: 让我看看，我正在打开网页。

sentences.en: Person with a beard, um, star eyes, zebra, giraffe.
sentences.zh: 留胡子的人，嗯，星星眼，斑马，长颈鹿。

sentences.en: The hijab emoji passed, that's really cool.
sentences.zh: 头巾表情符号通过了，这真的很酷。

sentences.en: Um, I'm not seeing mine.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我没看到我的。

sentences.en: Person, uh, serious face with symbols covering mouth, face with open mouth vomiting.
sentences.zh: 人，嗯，嘴上贴着符号的严肃脸，捂嘴呕吐的脸。

sentences.en: Ooh, that's, um, person in steamy room, person climbing, person in lotus position for yoga and meditation.
sentences.zh: 哦，那个是，嗯，蒸气室里的人，攀爬的人，盘腿打坐瑜伽的人。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 那很好。

sentences.en: It passed.
sentences.zh: 它通过了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: There we go.
sentences.zh: 这就对了。

sentences.en: So that's it.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这样。

sentences.en: Yours passed.
sentences.zh: 你的通过了。

sentences.en: And more importantly, Ryu's passed.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，Ryu的也通过了。

sentences.en: That's so great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah, both of ours were accepted, and I am super excited about it, as you could probably tell.
sentences.zh: 对，我们俩的都被接受了，我对此超级兴奋，你可能也看得出来。

sentences.en: So they, they changed the name of mine from person meditating to person in lotus position.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把我的名字从“打坐的人”改成了“盘腿而坐的人”。

sentences.en: You know, Unicode really likes the specificity of these things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，统一码联盟真的很喜欢这些东西的具体性。

sentences.en: And as of now, we're recording in August of 2017.
sentences.zh: 截至目前，我们是在2017年8月进行录制的。

sentences.en: It's not on your phone just yet.
sentences.zh: 它现在还不在你的手机里。

sentences.en: But person in lotus position, the hijab emoji, and all these new ones should be on your phone by the end of the year.
sentences.zh: 但是盘腿而坐的人、头巾表情符号和所有这些新表情符号应该在年底前就会出现在你的手机上了。

sentences.en: So when you get the person in lotus position emoji on your phone, you can think of Mark and how he doesn't even like yoga.
sentences.zh: 所以当你在手机上收到盘腿而坐的人表情符号时，你可以想起马克以及他甚至都不喜欢瑜伽这件事。

sentences.en: No, but that's, that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 不，但是，这就是重点所在。

sentences.en: I actually have started doing yoga and meditation now.
sentences.zh: 我其实已经开始练习瑜伽和冥想了。

sentences.en: It's one of the many things that came out of doing this story for me.
sentences.zh: 这是我做这个故事所带来的众多收获之一。

sentences.en: A huge new appreciation of yoga and meditation.
sentences.zh: 对瑜伽和冥想产生了巨大的全新赏识。

sentences.en: Well, that's remarkable.
sentences.zh: 哇，那真是非同寻常。

sentences.en: Well, then namaste for real then.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我就郑重地说一声合十礼吧。

sentences.en: Namaste, Roman.
sentences.zh: 合十礼，罗曼。

sentences.en: You know, that just means hello, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那只是代表你好，对吧？

sentences.en: More emoji talk after these fine people pay for our listening experience.
sentences.zh: 在这些优秀的人为我们的听觉体验买单之后，还有更多关于表情符号的讨论。

sentences.en: Raised hands.
sentences.zh: 举起双手。

sentences.en: Our female dancing bunnies versus our male dancing bunnies, we made the decision that they're wearing the exact same outfit.
sentences.zh: 我们的女性兔子舞者与我们的男性兔子舞者，我们决定让他们穿一模一样的衣服。

sentences.en: Men get the skimpy leotard just like the ladies.
sentences.zh: 男士们也像女士们一样穿暴露的连体紧身衣。

sentences.en: Really, gender, a lot of it is a social construct.
sentences.zh: 真的，性别很大程度上是一种社会建构。

sentences.en: And if we're trying to be more universal, it's sometimes good to eliminate some of the social constructs so it doesn't feel super resonant for one culture over another.
sentences.zh: 如果我们试图变得更具普遍性，有时消除一些社会建构是很好的，这样它就不会对某一种文化产生过分强烈的共鸣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Also, I just have to say that men and dancing men with bunny ears is one of my favorite emojis at this point.
sentences.zh: 另外，我不得不说，男士和戴着兔耳朵跳舞的男士是目前我最喜欢的表情符号之一。

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: I love that we kept the man wearing a little leotard instead of putting shorts on him.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们让男人穿着小连体衣而不是给他穿短裤。

sentences.en: That was one of the best moments of my career.
sentences.zh: 那是我职业生涯中最棒的时刻之一。

sentences.en: I'm kidding.
sentences.zh: 我开玩笑的。

sentences.en: But I do think it's great.
sentences.zh: 但我确实觉得这很棒。

sentences.en: I do think it's a great decision that we made.
sentences.zh: 我确实觉得我们做出了一个绝佳的决定。

sentences.zh: 这个故事改编自马克的播客《欢迎来到麦金塔》，他目前正在该节目中播出关于表情符号的系列节目。

sentences.zh: 它的内容比我们能塞进这25分钟里的要深得多，所以如果你还有什么想知道的，你知道的，关于表情符号的事情，

sentences.en: they're probably answered in this series.
sentences.zh: 这个系列里大概都有解答。

sentences.zh: 第一集现在已经上线了。

sentences.zh: 你可以在Macintosh.fm或你收听播客的任何地方找到它。

sentences.zh: 这个节目还有很多关于设计和技术的其他单集，你们这些可爱的极客一定会喜欢的。

sentences.zh: 我们委托卡拉·罗斯·德法比奥创作了原创表情符号艺术，完全用表情符号讲述了这一集的完整故事。
